lines.t: In this town, while everyone is practicing shouting, I'm practicing whispering. Hush, hush, hush.
Because every summer, this town has the Big Shout Festival. The loudest voice wins the golden trophy.
My friend Benny shouts his breakfast order.
The baker shouts at his bread.
Even my grandma shouts at the TV. And it's not even on.
But me? I wake up at five AM and tiptoe across the creakiest floor in the house. Two hundred times. Before breakfast.
I whisper the cat to sleep. Then the dog. Then my alarm clock. Hush, hush, hush.
I walk past my sister's room so quietly, she still thinks I moved out.
The whole town laughs at me. They call me Whisper Boy.
Nobody ever won a trophy for being quiet!
Then comes festival day. The whole town is in the square. The Mayor climbs on stage with his megaphone.
Ready... set... SHOUT!
Everyone screams at once. Windows rattle. Birds fly away. The clock tower shakes.
And under the stage... something wakes up.
A bear. A huge, grumpy, very sleepy bear.
Everyone freezes. Then they do the worst thing possible. They scream louder.
The louder they scream, the angrier it gets. It roars at the Mayor. The Mayor drops his megaphone.
But me? I've been training for this my whole life.
I tiptoe across the stage. Not one creak. Hush, hush, hush.
I whisper to the bear, just like I whisper to my cat.
Its eyes get heavy. It yawns. And it curls up and falls asleep. Right on top of the golden trophy.
For the first time in a hundred years, this town is silent.
So the Mayor gave the trophy to me. Well, after the bear moved.
And next year, the festival has a new name. The Big Whisper.
Benny asked me how I did it. I said: while you were shouting, I was practicing. Hush, hush, hush.
